title: Rumoured 6,000-Piece LEGO Icons Set: What Could It Be?
summary: A rumour points to a huge new LEGO Icons set landing later this year, and fans are already speculating about what it might be. Here's what's being said, clearly flagged as unconfirmed.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A rumour circulating online suggests LEGO Icons could be getting a massive new set numbered 11388, reportedly weighing in at 5,682 pieces. According to the rumour, it could launch this November with a price around €499.99.

None of this has been confirmed by the LEGO Group, so treat the set number, piece count, price and release window as **rumour only** for now.

Off the back of this, some fan speculation has emerged about what the set could actually be, since LEGO Icons covers everything from landmarks to licensed builds to retro throwbacks. Suggestions floated (again, purely speculative and not confirmed) include a giant Space Invaders arcade cabinet, in the style of existing Icons arcade sets like 10323 PAC-MAN Arcade and 11374 Arcade Pinball Machine, and an architectural build of Mont-Saint-Michel, the famous French tidal island, which could suit the scale of a nearly 6,000-piece set.

## Why it matters
LEGO Icons is one of the most popular themes for adult builders, collectors and display fans, so any hint of a new large-scale set generates a lot of interest. A set at this size and price point would be a major release for the theme, and speculation like this gives fans a fun way to imagine what might be coming, even before anything is official.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for any official confirmation from the LEGO Group regarding set 11388, including its actual theme, piece count, price and release date. Until then, all details remain unverified rumour.

title: Second LEGO minifigure element found cracking in September 2026 wave
summary: Fans have spotted hairline cracks on the new Gingy head piece from 71053 Shrek Minifigures, days after similar cracks appeared on the new Patrick head from the SpongeBob set.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Collectors opening 71053 Shrek Minifigures are reporting hairline cracks on Gingy's new head element. Photos shared by several fans online show the cracks running down the middle of the head mould, appearing on the front, top and back of the piece.

This follows earlier reports of cracking on the new head sculpt used for Patrick in 11386 SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom, though those cracks were reportedly limited to the back of the head. Brick Fanatics says its own copy of the Gingy minifigure also showed the same crack when checked.

It's worth noting Gingy's head is a brand-new element for this set, not the older gingerbread piece used previously, which has not had this issue. As of now, there's been no official statement from the LEGO Group addressing the cracks in either minifigure.

## Why it matters
Two new head elements cracking within the same wave of September 2026 sets points to a possible quality issue in production, rather than isolated bad luck. For collectors chasing complete, undamaged sets — especially those buying multiples to secure a full minifigure collection — this is worth watching before buying in bulk.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for any official response from the LEGO Group confirming or explaining the cracks, and watch whether other minifigures using new head sculpts in this wave show the same problem. If you've bought 71053 Shrek, it's worth checking your own Gingy minifigure closely.

title: LEGO PlayStation: how the 1,911-piece set compares to the original console
summary: A first close-up look at LEGO's 72306 PlayStation reveals it's a near 1:1 scale recreation of Sony's original console, complete with working buttons and opening disc lid.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has shared a first official look at 72306 PlayStation, a 1,911-piece LEGO set due out early next month, comparing it directly to Sony's original grey console.

The brick-built version measures over 6cm high, 26cm wide and 19cm deep, closely matching the real PS1's dimensions. It includes a brick-built DualShock controller (only one included, but it plugs into either front port), a spring-loaded disc lid that pops open via a press of the Open button, and two pull-out game dioramas hidden inside. A Power button on the left activates a small element to simulate the console lighting up. The two front memory card slots appear to be non-functional, and there's no confirmation yet of a brick-built memory card accessory.

The set's packaging is also said to closely echo Sony's original box design, with a strip of brick elements along the bottom typical of LEGO's 18+ range.

## Why it matters
This is shaping up to be one of the most detailed nostalgia-driven LEGO builds yet, blending display appeal with genuine playable mechanisms. For collectors and display builders, the near 1:1 scale and functional details (opening lid, buttons) make it a standout piece for retro gaming shelves alongside other 18+ sets.

## What to watch next
Expect further official reveals as the release date approaches, including full pricing, exact piece count confirmation, and whether any additional accessories (like a memory card) are included.

The LEGO Group and Sony have officially confirmed 72306 PlayStation, a 1,911-piece brick recreation of the classic 1994 console, complete with a buildable DualShock controller.

This is a rare official crossover between LEGO and a major gaming brand, appealing to both LEGO collectors and retro gaming fans. The hidden diorama Easter eggs also showcase clever building techniques that could inspire custom builders and display enthusiasts.

title: LEGO PlayStation set sparks fan backlash over timing and game choices
summary: The newly revealed LEGO PlayStation set has divided fans, with jokes about Sony's shift away from physical media and criticism of the chosen in-box video game dioramas.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has revealed 72306 PlayStation, its latest brick-built retro console model, continuing a series that has previously covered other classic gaming hardware. The reveal has prompted a strong reaction from fans online, largely focused on two points: the timing of a physical LEGO tribute to the PlayStation shortly after news that Sony is moving away from physical media, and the choice of games featured in the set's two internal dioramas, which depict Ape Escape and Gran Turismo.

According to reports, Reddit users have been quick to joke about the irony, with comments suggesting the set should have been digital-only in keeping with Sony's direction. Other fans have questioned the accuracy of the Ape Escape diorama, noting the controller shown isn't the DualShock associated with that game, and have suggested other titles such as Crash Bandicoot, Metal Gear Solid, Twisted Metal, Final Fantasy 7, Resident Evil, Tekken or Tomb Raider might have been more fitting choices to represent the console's legacy.

## Why it matters
LEGO's collaborations with iconic tech and gaming brands tend to generate strong interest among adult fans and collectors, so community reaction like this can shape expectations for future licensed sets. It's also a reminder that fan feedback on set contents, from included minifigures to diorama choices, can be vocal and detailed, which may influence how LEGO approaches similar collaborations going forward.

## What to watch next
It remains to be seen whether LEGO or Sony respond publicly to the fan commentary, and further official details on 72306 PlayStation's price, release date and full contents are still awaited.

LEGO designer Ellen Bowley has confirmed to Brick Fanatics and other fan media that the newly announced 21371 Wallace & Gromit set contains an Easter egg referencing Feathers McGraw, the silent penguin villain from *The Wrong Trousers* and *Vengeance Most Fowl*.

title: LEGO reveals why Wallace & Gromit's ladder didn't make the cut
summary: LEGO designer Ellen Bowley has explained why the upcoming 21371 Wallace & Gromit Ideas set skips the iconic ladder from A Close Shave, leaving room for fans to build their own.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Ahead of the launch of 21371 Wallace & Gromit, LEGO designer Ellen Bowley has addressed a question fans have been asking: where's the ladder?

The set recreates the motorcycle and sidecar from A Close Shave, based on fan designer Sébastien Esnault's winning LEGO Ideas submission. The ladder is a memorable feature of the film and appears on promotional artwork and other licensed merchandise, so its absence stood out to some fans.

Speaking to Brick Fanatics and other LEGO fan media at a roundtable, Bowley explained that the decision came from Aardman itself. The studio wanted a "clean" and "sleek" look for the model, and the specific reference vehicle used didn't feature a ladder either. Bowley said the team did experiment with including it, but ultimately left it off to give builders the chance to add their own personal touches instead.

21371 Wallace & Gromit is set to launch on 1 October for £89.99 / $99.99 / €99.99.

## Why it matters
This is a useful reminder that official licensed LEGO sets often go through approval from the source studio, not just LEGO's own design team - in this case Aardman had direct creative input on the final look. For fans and collectors, it also opens the door to a fun customisation project, since adding a ladder is a relatively simple build.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for fan-made ladder MOCs once the set is in more people's hands from 1 October - it could become a popular small addition or accessory build within the community.

title: LEGO Ideas Wallace & Gromit set uses newly developed printed dome eyes
summary: LEGO designers reveal that 21371 Wallace & Gromit required brand new printing technology to create printed 1x1 dome eye pieces, rather than the usual flat printed tiles.

According to the designers, the 1x1 dome piece existed before but wasn't previously printable. Ellen Bowley added that the graphic design team tried numerous approaches to get the print working on the curved element, with a flat-tile version kept as a backup in case it didn't succeed.

## Why it matters
This shows LEGO investing in new manufacturing techniques specifically to nail small details on a licensed Ideas set, rather than settling for existing elements. For fans of buildable figures, character models and printing techniques, it signals a level of craftsmanship that could influence future minifigure and character-based designs.
